summary: Anna Aurelia Esposito is an Indologist who studied at Heidelberg, Würzburg, and Tübingen (MA, 1998). She served as an assistant professor at the University of Würzburg (attested 2012–2015) and later joined the University of Zurich as PD Dr. (attested 2026).

Anna Balikci-Denjongpa works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS under Lionel Caplan, also studying with traditional teachers Lopen Dugyal and Gorlok Tulku, and became Research Coordinator at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology in 2002.

Anna Brown is a scholar in religious studies and other fields who studied Zen under Robert Kennedy (attested 2017). As of 2017, she served at Saint Peter's University as chair of political science and director of social justice.

Anna Filigenzi is a scholar of archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. A member of IsMEO from 1984, she directed the Italian Archaeological Mission in Afghanistan (2003) and held posts at Naples "L'Orientale" (~2012) and Naples Federico II (attested 2021).
Anna M. Shields is a sinologist who held posts at the University of Maryland, College Park (~2007–2015), and Princeton University (~2015).
Anna Morpurgo Davies was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1955–1959) and held an academic post at the University of Oxford from around 1964 to 2004.

Anna Sawerthal is a scholar of Tibetology. She completed an MA at the University of Vienna under Klaus-Dieter Mathes, with Johanna Buß, and later earned a PhD at Heidelberg University, studying under Dawa Tsering and Norbu Tashi.

Anna Seidel was a scholar of sinology and religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and under Max Kaltenmark and Rolf Alfred Stein. She joined EFEO (1969), worked at Institut du Hōbōgirin (~1970–1991), and founded Cahiers d'Extrême-Asie in 1985.

Anna Szabolcsi is a linguist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (PhD). She worked at the Hungarian Research Centre for Linguistics (~1976–1990), UCLA (~1990–1998), and became professor of linguistics at NYU (~1998).

Anna-Pya Sjödin is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. She earned her PhD from Uppsala University in 2007, where her doctoral supervisors included Gunilla Gren-Eklund, Eli Franco, Jonardon Ganeri, K. Venugopalan, and Toshihiro Wada, with additional instruction from Barbro Eriksson.
Annarao Kulkarni is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology. He has held positions at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing and the Indian Heritage Language Computing Group.

Anne C. Klein is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. Educated at Binghamton, Wisconsin-Madison, and Virginia (PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins), she founded Dawn Mountain (~1996) and became Professor and Chair of Religious Studies at Rice University (~1987).

Anne Casile is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied under Claudine Bautze-Picron. She served as an AHRC research assistant at the British Museum (~2005–2009) and joined the French National Research Institute for Sustainable Development (~2012).

Anne E. Monius was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned undergraduate, master's, and doctoral degrees at Harvard. She taught at the University of Virginia (1997–2002) before returning to Harvard University as professor of South Asian Religions in 2002.

Anne Farrer is a scholar of sinology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She served as Assistant Keeper in the Department of Oriental Antiquities at the British Museum and held a post at Sotheby's Institute of Art (attested 2005).

Anne Feldhaus is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies who studied at Manhattanville University and earned her doctorate from the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). In 1981, she joined Arizona State University, becoming Distinguished Foundation Professor and later Emeritus Professor.

Anne Hardgrove is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Carleton College (~1986–1990) and the University of Michigan (~1991–1999), and joined the University of Texas at San Antonio in 2000.
Anne Hopkins Aitken was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who co-founded the Honolulu Diamond Sangha in 1959 and founded the Maui Zendo.

Anne M. Blackburn is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Chicago (1991) and held appointments as Assistant Professor at Cornell University (~2000) and later as Professor at Harvard University.

Anne MacDonald is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of British Columbia under Shotaro Iida. She has held posts at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (attested 2012) and the University of Vienna (attested 2008, 2026).
